events.title: Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum
events.description: By the traditional date, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice, killing thousands. Some evidence suggests October; the ruins preserve a unique picture of Roman life.
events.html: By the traditional date, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice, killing thousands. Some evidence suggests October; the ruins preserve a unique picture of Roman life.

events.title: Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome
events.description: The Visigoths under Alaric entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time the city had fallen to a foreign enemy in some 800 years. The shock prompted Augustine's City of God.
events.html: The Visigoths under Alaric entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time the city had fallen to a foreign enemy in some 800 years. The shock prompted Augustine's City of God.

events.title: British troops burn Washington
events.description: After routing American militia at Bladensburg, British forces entered Washington and set fire to the Capitol and the President's House. It was partly revenge for the American burning of York.
events.html: After routing American militia at Bladensburg, British forces entered Washington and set fire to the Capitol and the President's House. It was partly revenge for the American burning of York.

events.title: Amelia Earhart flies non-stop across the United States
events.description: Amelia Earhart flew from Los Angeles to Newark in about 19 hours, the first woman to cross the continent non-stop. That May she had become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
events.html: Amelia Earhart flew from Los Angeles to Newark in about 19 hours, the first woman to cross the continent non-stop. That May she had become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

events.title: Microsoft launches Windows 95
events.description: Microsoft released Windows 95 with a huge marketing campaign; customers queued at midnight. Its Start menu and taskbar set the pattern of the personal computer desktop for decades.
